findings.title: Destructive tool exposes no authorization surface
findings.description: The tool appears to mutate state or move money, but its schema declares no confirmation, approval-token, or dry-run argument. Execution is gated only on the model choosing to call it.
findings.remediation: Add a confirmation or authorization argument (or a dry_run default) to every state-mutating tool, and enforce it server-side - not just in the schema.

findings.title: Unbounded string parameter
findings.description: Parameter 'path' accepts a string with no maximum length, enum, or pattern. It can carry arbitrarily large or arbitrary content into the tool - including flood payloads and injection strings.
findings.remediation: Constrain 'path' with maxLength and/or a pattern or enum.

findings.title: Numeric parameter without range
findings.description: Parameter 'expected_replacements' is numeric with no minimum or maximum. Out-of-range values (negative amounts, absurd quantities) reach the tool.
findings.remediation: Declare minimum/maximum for 'expected_replacements'.

findings.title: State-mutating tool declares no required arguments
findings.description: The tool can mutate state while every argument is optional. The agent can invoke it with an empty or degenerate call, and the schema communicates no intended shape.
findings.remediation: Mark the arguments the tool genuinely needs as required.
